pagination.note: Page size is fixed at 30 (no per_page override). The pool's 29 plans (top-level only: 15, since one holds 14 sub-plans) never exceeds 30, so a genuine second page of real data cannot be produced from this pool under any parameter combination -- confirmed structurally, not just by observation.

branch_include_sub_plans.drift: info.count stayed at 15 (top-level-only count) even though the array grew to 29 rows once sub-plans were included. The declared schema says info.count is 'Total number of items' -- it tracks the top-level filter scope, not len(test_plans), so it silently disagrees with the array it's paginating whenever include_sub_plans=true is used.

branch_page_beyond_data.note: Envelope shape identical to the single-page branch (page, page_size, count, prev, next all present; prev correctly populated, next correctly null). No total_pages/prev/next inconsistency here -- unlike the tracked list_workspace_fields_v2 defect, this capability's info envelope is stable and matches the declared required set across all three branches probed.

pagination.verdict_on_known_defect_class: NOT PRESENT. This capability does not exhibit the list_workspace_fields_v2-style envelope drift (dropping total_pages / adding undeclared prev-next only on multi-page). Its info shape is fixed and matches contract across all observed branches. The real drift found here is different: info.count desyncs from the actual row count when include_sub_plans changes what's in the array (see branch_include_sub_plans above).

v1_vs_v2.id_form: v1 rows carry both a numeric `id` (what every other v1 plan route needs) and the display `identifier` (TP-NNN/STP-NNN). v2 rows carry ONLY `identifier` -- there is no numeric id field at all; the numeric project/plan ids are recoverable only by parsing them out of the `urls.self` web-app link.
v1_vs_v2.project_id_param: v1 path takes the numeric project_id (e.g. 379335744). v2 path requires the PR-NNN string form (regex-constrained ^PR-\d+$) -- a bare integer never matches the v2 route.
v1_vs_v2.filtering: v1 supports status, sort_by, q (free text/tags/ids/owner/team/custom-fields/date filters), include_sub_plans, minify, filter_mapping, filter_details, ignore_type. v2 has NONE of this -- only p and count/page_size. v2's own guidance says to filter client-side or fall back to v1.
v1_vs_v2.page_size: v1: fixed at 30, no override parameter exists. v2: default 30, overridable via `count` (or `page_size` alias) up to a hard ceiling of 300 (400 above that, not clamped); v2 also caps deep paging at 30,000 rows via a 429.
v1_vs_v2.envelope: Both declare the same info{page,page_size,count,prev,next} shape. v1 additionally returns a project-wide `count`{active,completed} rollup at the top level that v2 does not have at all.
v1_vs_v2.row_shape: v1 rows are the full plan object (owner, assignee, created_by, custom_fields, test_plan_progress_v2, record_status, review_status, links, etc). v2 rows are slimmer: no owner/assignee/created_by/custom_fields/progress/record_status -- just identifier, name, description, active_state, tags, issues, test_runs_count, sub_plans_count, parent_plan_id, start/end/created_at, project_id (as PR-NNN), and urls{self, sub_test_plans}.
v1_vs_v2.parent_plan_id_semantics: v1: integer, key always present, null on a top-level plan. v2: string TP-NNN identifier, and the key is ABSENT ENTIRELY on a top-level plan (never returned as null) -- opposite null-vs-absent convention from v1.
v1_vs_v2.preferred_or_deprecated: Neither describeCapability record carries a preferred/deprecated flag or any cross-reference to the other. They are an unlabelled near-duplicate pair: same intent ('list a project's test plans'), same route family, materially different id space, params and row shape, with no contract signal steering a caller to one over the other.

undeclared_returned: test_plans[].test_plan_progress (always {}, separate from the declared test_plan_progress_v2)

notes: Capability works end to end and the request/response mechanics (path param, p, include_sub_plans, envelope) all behave as documented. Verdict is DRIFT rather than PASS for two reasons: (1) six row-level fields (completed_by, test_plan_progress, test_results_trend, test_results_trend_v2, attachments, review_status) are returned on every row but are absent from the capability's declared `returns` list -- an undeclared-field gap in the same class the registry's returns/schema build check is meant to catch. (2) info.count silently desyncs from len(test_plans) once include_sub_plans=true pulls extra rows into the array -- the field keeps reporting the top-level-only total, not the count of what's actually being paginated. Separately, sub-plan rows (fetched via include_sub_plans=true) return null for a cluster of fields the schema types as plain (non-nullable) string/object/array -- plan_status, tags, issues, created_by, owner, assignee, record_status, start_date, end_date, created_at, updated_at, sub_plans_count, test_plan_progress_v2 were all null on the STP-* rows -- an undeclared-nullability gap, shallowest path: test_plans[].tags (typed {type:array}, no nullable, observed null). Pagination itself is clean: the known list_workspace_fields_v2-style envelope-drift defect does NOT reproduce here across single-page, sub-plans-inflated, and beyond-data-page branches; genuinely could not force a real second page of data since the pool's 29 items never exceed the fixed page size of 30 under any filter combination. v1 vs v2 is a real unlabelled-duplicate case: different id space (numeric id vs identifier-only), different project_id form (int vs PR-NNN), v1 has rich filtering v2 lacks entirely, and neither carries a preferred/deprecated marker.
